name: Asal Forouzandeh
bio: Asal is a postdoctoral researcher in the Microbial Genomics & Biodegradation group. She works on the discovery and characterisation of PFAS-degrading microbes and enzymes. Her work involves screening environmental isolates for PFAS-degrading activity and identifying the enzymes responsible. She develops and validates fluoride-release assays and steady-state kinetics to characterise newly discovered PFAS-active enzymes against fluorinated substrates, supporting the lab's enzyme-based remediation efforts. Her current project maps microbial community structure across contaminated sites around Denmark and links bacterial community composition to PFAS contamination. Asal brings a strong background in environmental microbiology and molecular techniques. This was built during a PhD on how high dietary copper shapes the intestinal microbiota and resistome of pigs and broilers, including the co-selection of antibiotic resistance by metals.
